svg.title: Allocate Startup Cash Without Treating Inventory as Profit
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-startup-capital-allocation; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Allocate Startup Cash Without Treating Inventory as Profit; subtitle: Four buckets total $100,000 within the $10,000–$150,000 range.; chapter number: 4; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: This is one illustrative $100,000 opening cash allocation, not a required portfolio size or an annual expense forecast. Numeric values are dollars; labels show shares of the same capital pool. Do not add these buckets to the annual waterfall as though all cash deployed were current expense.; caption: $50,000 + $10,000 + $10,000 + $30,000 = $100,000. At $500–$5,000 monthly operating expense, the $30,000 operating reserve covers 6–60 months before inventory purchases and separately reserved renewals.; stages: label: Acquisition inventory; value: $50,000; 50% of opening capital; numeric value: 50000.0; detail: Deploy gradually into researched names and capped auction bids; retain a per-domain basis ledger rather than marking unsold inventory to asking prices.; label: Research and transaction setup; value: $10,000; 10% of opening capital; numeric value: 10000.0; detail: Reserve for comparable-sale tools, historical-use research, targeted rights review, and initial transaction setup; release funds against scoped work.; label: Renewal and transfer reserve; value: $10,000; 10% of opening capital; numeric value: 10000.0; detail: Ring-fence cash against registrar renewal schedules, premium-name charges, and transfer costs; revise the reserve as holdings and renewal dates change.; label: Operating runway reserve; value: $30,000; 30% of opening capital; numeric value: 30000.0; detail: Support contractor work, inquiry handling, and routine administration while sales remain uneven; six months at maximum operating expense falls short of the 24-month first-deal horizon.
